findings.issue: permanentClientError sends 401 and 403 to DEAD at once, as well as 400 and 422. A 401 or 403 from cart-service's /internal/** chain means the X-Internal-Token is wrong or blank, which is a configuration or rotation fault and not a fault in the payload. During a token rotation window, or after a bad deploy, every CLEAR_CART row would go DEAD on its first relay attempt instead of retrying until the fault is fixed. This fails safe because no cart line is wrongly removed, and the runbook says replaying DEAD CLEAR_CART rows is harmless. Outside callers cannot use it to drop another user's clear: the status depends only on the service token and on the stored payload, which was built from the user's own validated cart, so at worst a user stops their own cart from being cleared.
findings.fix: Optional: also leave 401 and 403 out of the permanent set, so only 400, 409, 413 and 422 go DEAD at once. Or keep the rule and add a line to the runbook that a burst of DEAD CLEAR_CART rows with 401 or 403 in last_error means the internal token is wrong, and that the rows should be replayed after it is fixed.

summary: All three earlier minor findings are fixed at b7f5b97. (1) NoUserTokenFeignConfig is a plain class, not @Configuration, and is referenced only from CartInternalFeignClient's configuration, so its Capability bean lives only in the cartInternalClient child context. The other InternalFeignConfig clients and the global DependencyBreakerCapability are not affected. Its Capability.enrich wraps every RequestInterceptor so that the interceptor runs first and Authorization is removed afterwards. RequestTemplate headers are case-insensitive, so the header is gone whatever order the interceptors run in. CartInternalFeignClientHeadersTest checks that the request carries X-Internal-Token and no Authorization inside a request context, and checks that the bearer leaks when the stripper is off. Evidence item 2 shows the guard fails when the removal is disabled. (2) removeConsumed now calls lockCartIfExists, a bound-parameter SELECT id ... FOR UPDATE with no insert, and returns 0 when no cart exists, so a relay or admin retry never creates a cart for an erased or unknown user. noCartCreatesNothing checks this and fails on 71bba97. (3) The CLEAR_CART payload retention is documented in the runbook's Data retention section and registered as TD-BE-19 (README row and backend.md entry). The new error handling is safe. OrderRemote.clearCart catches an enqueue failure and logs only the orderId and e.toString() of the outbox exception. That message holds SQL with placeholders and, at most, the database error text. It has no email, name or address. place() is not @Transactional on the COD and CARD path, so catching the exception does not leave a transaction marked rollback-only or aborted. The WALLET path still enqueues inside its tx.execute, so its atomicity is unchanged. COD ordering: the payment record is created before both the event and the clear, and only the ORDER_PLACED publish now comes before clearCart. The money path is unchanged, and an enqueue failure can no longer skip the placed event (enqueueFailureDoesNotFailACodOrder). The 409 fingerprint conflict is kept (enqueueFailureKeepsTheConflict). The 4xx-to-DEAD rule applies only to CLEAR_CART FeignExceptions and retries 404, 408, 429 and 5xx. It cannot be triggered across users. The one residual point, that 401 and 403 also go DEAD at once, is a minor operational concern. No new dependencies, secrets, endpoints or queries were added beyond the parameterised lock query.
